NumPy style universal functions

Source: R/numpy_ufuncs.R
jnp_ufunc.Rd

Port of jax.numpy.ufunc. jnp_ufunc() wraps an elementwise function func of nin arrays returning nout arrays (a list when nout > 1) into a callable ufunc object; calling it broadcasts the inputs and maps func over every element (with vmap()) unless a vectorized call is supplied. jnp_frompyfunc() is jnp.frompyfunc. The ufunc methods of JAX are the functions jnp_ufunc_reduce() (ufunc.reduce), jnp_ufunc_accumulate(), jnp_ufunc_reduceat(), jnp_ufunc_outer() and jnp_ufunc_at(); they are also reachable with $, as in jnp_ufuncs$add$reduce(x), and u$nin, u$nout, u$nargs, u$identity and u$name give the properties.

Usage

jnp_ufunc(
  func,
  nin,
  nout,
  name = NULL,
  nargs = NULL,
  identity = NULL,
  call = NULL,
  reduce = NULL,
  accumulate = NULL,
  at = NULL,
  reduceat = NULL
)

jnp_frompyfunc(func, nin, nout, identity = NULL)

jnp_ufunc_reduce(
  ufunc,
  a,
  axis = 0L,
  dtype = NULL,
  out = NULL,
  keepdims = FALSE,
  initial = NULL,
  where = NULL
)

jnp_ufunc_accumulate(ufunc, a, axis = 0L, dtype = NULL, out = NULL)

jnp_ufunc_reduceat(ufunc, a, indices, axis = 0L, dtype = NULL, out = NULL)

jnp_ufunc_outer(ufunc, A, B)

jnp_ufunc_at(ufunc, a, indices, b = NULL, inplace = TRUE)

# S3 method for class 'jnp_ufunc'
x$name

# S3 method for class 'jnp_ufunc'
print(x, ...)

Arguments

func

Elementwise function of nin arguments.

nin, nout

Number of inputs and outputs.

name

Name of the ufunc (by default the name of func or "<lambda>"); for $, the property or method name.

nargs

Number of arguments (default nin).

identity

Identity element of a binary ufunc, or NULL.

call, reduce, accumulate, at, reduceat

Optional specialized implementations.

ufunc

A ufunc object.

a, A, B

Arrays.

axis

Axis (0-based); NULL reduces over all axes in jnp_ufunc_reduce().

dtype

Optional result dtype.

out

Not supported (must be NULL).

keepdims

Keep reduced dimensions with size one.

initial

Initial value of the reduction.

where

Boolean mask of the elements to reduce.

indices

Indices (see Details).

b

Second operand of at for binary ufuncs.

inplace

Must be FALSE (JAX arrays are immutable).

x

A ufunc object.

...

Ignored.

Value

jnp_ufunc() and jnp_frompyfunc() return a ufunc object; the methods return arrays.

Details

Axes are 0-based. indices of jnp_ufunc_at() is one index (see at_get()) or a plain list of indices, one per dimension (a Python tuple). As in JAX, at cannot operate in place: pass inplace = FALSE and use the result.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
jnp_ufuncs$add$reduce(jnp_arange(5))
u <- jnp_frompyfunc(function(x, y) x * y + 1, nin = 2, nout = 1, identity = 0)
jnp_ufunc_outer(u, c(1, 2), c(3, 4, 5))
} # }
